Job Description
Gas Turbine Electrical Systems Technicians operate the electric plant and main propulsion control equipment; locate circuit failures and replace parts;
measure current, voltage and resistance; test for shorts, grounds and continuity; test protective circuitry; test, service, and replace batteries; perform
preventative and corrective maintenance on digital data equipment and control and monitor circuits; measure insulation resistance; repair
electrical/electronic cables, wiring, and connectors; maintain machinery control systems, and alarm, indicating and warning systems; construct operating
systems, and networking and Information Technology (IT) systems; maintain and repair Gas Turbine Engines (GTE), Main Reduction Gear (MRG), and
auxiliary equipment; work with blueprints, schematics, and charts; perform administrative procedures related to Gas Turbine (GT) propulsion system
operations and maintenance; perform work area inspections; operate standard test equipment; stop engines and check for proper performance; replace and
adjust operating tolerance of contacts, micro switches, relay switches, pressure switches, and temperature switches; work independently; and provide
limited guidance, support, and instruction to Gas Turbine Electrical Systems Maintainers.

Gas Turbine Electrical Systems Technicians operate the electric plant and main propulsion control equipment; locate circuit failures and replace parts; measure current, voltage and resistance; test for shorts, grounds and continuity; test protective circuitry; test, service, and replace batteries; perform preventative and corrective maintenance on digital data equipment and control and monitor circuits; measure insulation resistance; repair electrical/electronic cables, wiring, and connectors; maintain machinery control systems, and alarm, indicating and warning systems; construct operating systems, and networking and Information Technology (IT) systems; maintain and repair Gas Turbine Engines (GTE), Main Reduction Gear (MRG), and auxiliary equipment; work with blueprints, schematics, and charts; perform administrative procedures related to Gas Turbine (GT) propulsion system operations and maintenance; perform work area inspections; operate standard test equipment; stop engines and check for proper performance; replace and adjust operating tolerance of contacts, micro switches, relay switches, pressure switches, and temperature switches; work independently; and provide limited guidance, support, and instruction to Gas Turbine Electrical Systems Maintainers.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
